group.passage: Imagine drawing a little stick figure in the corner of each page of a notebook and then flipping the pages fast: the figure seems to move. Such a little book is called a flip book, and cartoons work on the same idea. In 1868, an English printer named John Barnes Linnett got a patent for a small book of pictures like this. He called it a kineograph, which means “moving picture.” The secret of a flip book is a trick of the eye: when pictures pass by quickly, our eyes cannot see them one by one, so they blend together into smooth movement. Each page works like one frame of a film, and each picture is only a little different from the one before it. In this way, the flip book pointed the way to motion pictures. Film gave artists a new way to make drawings move. In 1906, J. Stuart Blackton filmed himself drawing funny faces and then made the faces move. Not long after that, the French artist Emile Cohl made a short film from about 700 drawings. Even with so many pictures, it lasted less than two minutes. Some critics say that the first cartoon character with a personality of her own was a dinosaur. In 1914, Winsor McCay first showed Gertie the Dinosaur at a theater in Chicago. He stood on the stage with a whip and gave Gertie orders, and he even seemed to feed her an apple. Audiences at that time were not used to films, so many people believed Gertie was real. McCay also saved drawing time: to show Gertie breathing, he filmed the same set of drawings again and again, up to fifteen times. Over the years, cartoons grew longer. In 1937, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs became the first full-length cartoon film made in America, and more than 750 artists worked on it for about three years. Still, it used the same idea as the flip book: many pictures, each a bit different from the last, shown one after another.

translation_zh.text:
想像一下：在筆記本每一頁的角落畫一個小火柴人，然後快速翻動書頁——那個小人看起來就會動。這樣的小書叫做翻頁書，而卡通運用的也是同一個原理。1868 年，一位名叫約翰．巴恩斯．林奈特的英國印刷商替這樣一本小圖畫書取得了專利。他把它叫做 kineograph，意思是「會動的圖畫」。
翻頁書的祕密在於一種眼睛的錯覺：當圖畫很快地閃過時，我們的眼睛無法一張一張分開來看，於是它們就融合成流暢的動作。每一頁就像影片的一格畫面，而每張圖都只和前一張有一點點不同。就這樣，翻頁書為電影指出了方向。
影片讓藝術家有了讓圖畫動起來的新方法。1906 年，J．史都華．布萊克頓拍下自己畫滑稽臉孔的過程，然後讓那些臉孔動了起來。不久之後，法國藝術家埃米爾．科爾用大約 700 張圖畫做出一部短片。儘管用了這麼多張圖，片長卻不到兩分鐘。
有些評論者說，第一個擁有自己個性的卡通角色是一隻恐龍。1914 年，溫莎．麥凱在芝加哥的一家戲院首次放映《恐龍葛蒂》。他拿著鞭子站在舞台上對葛蒂下指令，甚至好像還餵她吃了一顆蘋果。當時的觀眾還不習慣看電影，所以許多人相信葛蒂是真的。麥凱也想辦法節省作畫的時間：為了表現葛蒂在呼吸，他把同一組圖畫反覆拍攝，最多拍了十五次。
這些年來，卡通越來越長。1937 年，《白雪公主與七矮人》成為美國第一部長篇卡通電影，有超過 750 位畫家花了大約三年製作。不過，它用的仍然是和翻頁書相同的原理：許多張圖畫，每張都和前一張有一點點不同，一張接一張地播放。
